message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas – Quick Reference Guide** | Topic | Key Points | Where to Find More Info | |-------|------------|------------------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits are the law.
• 55 mph on rural interstates, 65 mph on urban interstates, 45 mph on most highways.
• School zones: 25 mph (or 20 mph if posted).
• Construction zones: 35 mph unless otherwise posted. | Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT) – Speed Limit Regulations | | **Seat‑belt & Child Safety** | • All drivers and passengers must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child safety seat or booster.
• No “seat‑belt law” for teens; however, Texas has a “no‑seat‑belt” penalty for drivers under 18 if they’re not wearing a belt. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Cell‑Phone Use** | • Hand‑held phone use while driving is illegal.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed.
• Texting while driving is prohibited. | Texas Transportation Code §545.002 | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) of 0.08% or higher is illegal.
• Zero‑tolerance for drivers under 21 (BAC ≥ 0.02%).
• Penalties: fines, license suspension, possible jail time. | Texas Transportation Code §545.021 | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • Yield to pedestrians at crosswalks.
• Stop at stop signs and red lights.
• “Yield” signs give priority to the vehicle already in the intersection. | Texas Transportation Code §545.003 | | **School Bus Rules** | • Stop for a school bus with its stop‑light flashing and stop sign extended.
• Vehicles traveling in either direction must stop. | Texas Transportation Code §545.004 | | **Lane‑Changing & Overtaking** | • Use turn signals.
• Do not cut off other vehicles.
• “No‑passing” zones on two‑lane roads. | Texas Transportation Code §545.005 | | **Parking Regulations** | • No parking within 20 ft of a crosswalk, fire hydrant, or intersection.
• No parking in handicap spaces unless you have a valid permit. | Texas Transportation Code §545.006 | | **Vehicle Registration & Inspection** | • All vehicles must be registered and display a valid license plate.
• Most vehicles require an annual safety inspection. | Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV) | | **Insurance Requirements** | • Minimum liability coverage: $30,000 for bodily injury per person, $60,000 for total bodily injury, $25,000 for property damage. | Texas Insurance Code §151.001 | | **Special Situations** | • **Towing**: Must use a tow bar or chain; cannot tow a vehicle that is not in motion.
• **Emergency Vehicles**: Must yield to police, ambulance, and fire trucks. | Texas Transportation Code §545.007 | ### How to Stay Updated - **TxDOT**: [https://www.txdot.gov](https://www.txdot.gov) – for road rules, speed limits, and construction updates. - **Texas DMV**: [https://www.txdmv.gov](https://www.txdmv.gov) – for registration, insurance, and driver’s license info. - **Texas Legislature Online**: [https://capitol.texas.gov](https://capitol.texas.gov) – for the full text of the Texas Transportation Code. ### Quick Tips 1. **Always obey posted signs** – they override general rules. 2. **Use hands‑free** if you need to talk or use a GPS. 3. **Check your vehicle’s inspection status** before hitting the road. 4. **Keep your insurance documents** in the car; you may need to show them in an accident. Feel free to ask if you need details on a specific law or scenario!
